summary: Page 2 local-news page. Target item, "Echo Moves to Red Bank," reports that The Echo, a paper edited and published by W. E. Rack in the interest of the colored race in Long Branch, has relocated to Red Bank after Rack purchased a home there; he plans to run an industrial school for his race in Red Bank. Rest of page is routine Monmouth County local items (recitals, weddings, church notes, obituary-adjacent society notes) with no other Black-press content.

people.name: W. E. Rack
people.role: editor and publisher of The Echo, a Black-interest newspaper

incidents.what: The Echo newspaper relocates from Long Branch to Red Bank following editor W. E. Rack's purchase of a home there; Rack to establish an industrial school for Black residents in Red Bank

connections: The Echo (Long Branch/Red Bank), edited by W. E. Rack, is a Black-owned NJ newspaper of this period relevant to the project
